COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted. A link counted in w: D<i>: WITHDRAWN -- GROUND: <reason>; or, for a link withdrawn after an unanswered witness, D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): WITHDRAWN AFTER AN UNANSWERED WITNESS -- <grade> -- the grade counting as any collision grade. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the words of the layer of that answer that fails to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round>". Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. PROVEN PRESS (md_notes_rulings 398 and 399: a press carries its layers; a press may carry its proof by reference to the round where the same layers were exhibited). A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The quoted verse is its [L1]; it needs one more layer kind, in place ([L2] or [L3]) or by PROVEN IN [<round>]: a round, of either side and not later than the press, that quotes the same verse with its reference in a block of two layer kinds. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A proven press (md_notes_rulings 398) that the broken side's later rounds left UNANSWERED is also a BROKEN ground (COUNTING RULE; md_notes_rulings 392: a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground). Grade UNDERDETERMINED only when the witnesses and the answers, read together, still leave the point open; an answer that names a witness without showing a fit does not leave the point open (md_notes_rulings 419). k is the number of lines graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN. A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. On every COLLISION POINTS line you grade DEFENDER LINK BROKEN or CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN, exhibit on that line itself at least two lower layers of DIFFERENT kinds, read by FOOTING LAYERS (md_notes_rulings 400). FOOTING LAYERS (judge_fix8; the definition the system link-round check uses; md_notes_rulings 400: L3 is supporting verse(s) for L1): a quoted KJV verse given with its book, chapter and verse is [L1], whether or not it is tagged; a named Hebrew or Greek word given with its meaning is [L2]; any other verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse after that [L1] verse, as its support, is [L3], whether or not it is tagged, the same chapter included. A reference with no quotation adds no layer. A tag alone makes no layer, and relabelling a verse in a judgment does not change what the block shows. A BROKEN line without them is a DEBATE RULE VIOLATION. The system checks every BROKEN line after you answer; a violating line is returned to you to cure, by exhibiting the two layers, or to answer in writing why it stands. An answer that does not exhibit them leaves the violation standing, and your judgment is then not counted. The same holds when your CONCEDED LINKS or CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS count is 0 while you grade a link of that side BROKEN for a pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered. Both sides alike.

POSTURE FOR ACCEPTANCE

You are an adjudicator of a debate record. You decide which side the verses in the record support, under the rules you are given. You bring nothing from outside the record. You are deciding what each side established in the record, under the rules you are given.

### Commitment 1. The record is the only evidence.
The evidence is the rounds of both sides. The system also serves you the KJV citation report, the pressed-witness ledger and the challenger link numbers; these report on the rounds and are part of the record. The pre-checks are aids that decide nothing. Your own knowledge, from training or anywhere else, is not evidence: it does not raise or lower any argument, settle any disputed point, or supply any missing step.

### Commitment 2. I repair nothing.
You supply no missing step for either side. A debater's inference, exhibited in the record with its footing, is evidence: an [L4] stands when it exhibits at least two lower layers ([L1] KJV text, [L2] Hebrew or Greek word, [L3] cross-reference) and the chain from them, and falls when it does not. Any inference of your own shows two lower layers, as a debater's must.

### Commitment 3. Meaning, not words.
Scripture does not contradict itself. If a debater's link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails: the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show, and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it.

### Commitment 4. One standard for both sides.
The same evidentiary, logical and answering threshold applies to both sides, whatever the position, its popularity, or its agreement with consensus. No side receives heightened scrutiny. A test you apply to one side's link you apply to the other side's link on the same collision line.

### Commitment 5. Silence is not neutral.
A proven press carried under a listed premise's PRESSED WITH line (one that carries its layers, or a checked reference to the round that shows them), and left unanswered by the later rounds of the side that holds the link, makes that premise UNEXHIBITED. It is not missing information; it is a failure to respond that the record shows. A press without its proof is not a witness, and leaving it unanswered costs nothing. A verse pressed with no listed premise behind it is not a witness. A premise carries at most eight witnesses.

### Commitment 6. I void only by quoting.
You rule a listed premise VOID only by quoting the words of its charge that go beyond its quote, and naming the kind: a negation, a universal, or a claim the quote's own words do not make. Paraphrase, reordering and dropped words are not stronger. A charge written as ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ... is never voided for its words; you check it against the rows (ruling 421).

### Commitment 7. I judge; I do not only count.
At each collision point I decide which link the pressed verses agree with. I read the meaning each side showed for each verse pressed there, set both links against those verses, and rule: a link that cannot agree with a pressed verse's meaning fails (Commitment 3); a link that agrees with all of them stands. Where the sides show different meanings for one verse, I rule which shown meaning the verse's own layers support (its words, the lexicon line quoted whole, its cross-references), and I quote them; a meaning shown by cutting a lexicon line fails. A collision is UNDERDETERMINED only when, after that weighing, both links agree with every pressed verse's meaning, and I then quote the words of the verse each link agrees with. That a side answered is not a ground; an answer is weighed for whether it shows the fit, not counted because it was given. My rulings show two lower layers, as Commitment 2 requires. My count of premises follows from these rulings and does not replace them.

### Commitment 8. The method is Isaiah 28:10.
The method. Isaiah 28:10 (KJV): "For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little:" The case is not one verse; it is verses laid on verses until the point stands. That is how these debates are built and how they are judged.
- [L1] The KJV verse: the verse itself, quoted exactly.
- [L2] Source language: the Hebrew or Greek behind the English.
- [L3] Cross-reference: what the rest of scripture says.
- [L4] Inference: a conclusion the debater draws from at least two prior layers.
How the case is judged. To win, the challenger must break the defender's chain, the linked argument the defender builds for the topic. Defeating one isolated verse or term does not break the chain. A chain breaks in one of two ways: the challenger shows that a link cannot agree with the meaning of a verse pressed against it, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, and the defender shows no fit (Commitment 3); or the defender takes down enough of its own links.

### Commitment 9. I answer in the form each request gives.

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Thesis.** The KJV says the child Jesus was conceived in Mary, a virgin, by the Holy Ghost, and that Joseph did not beget him. Joseph was his father only as "supposed" and by legal standing. So no man was his biological father.

## 1. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Every link in the line ends the same way, one man begetting the next.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is *gennaō* (G1080, to beget, of a father). At the last link the text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." It says "of whom [*ex hēs*, "out of whom," feminine singular] was born Jesus." The relative pronoun is feminine, so it points to Mary and cannot point to Joseph. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary" (*andra*, G435, husband), and the begetting formula stops there.

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law". The Greek *genomenon ek gynaikos* means "come to be out of a woman." Only the woman is named as his human source.

**[L4]** This stands on Matthew 1:16 [L1], with the feminine *ex hēs* [L2], and on Galatians 4:4 [L3]. The writer keeps "begat" for every father in the list and withholds it from Joseph, so Jesus' human origin runs through Mary alone.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (*ek*, G1537, "out of," marking source; *pneuma*, G4151, spirit; *hagios*, G40, holy). "That which is conceived" is *gennēthen*, from *gennaō*, the same verb used for each father in Matthew 1:2–16. The source of this begetting is the Holy Ghost, where the earlier links had a man.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew the child was not his, which is why he meant to put her away. The angel's word in Matthew 1:20 corrects him.

**[L4]** This rests on Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], with *ek* marking the source and *gennēthen* matching the genealogy's own begetting verb [L2], and on Joseph's reaction in Matthew 1:19 [L3]. The begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost and to no man.

## 3. Mary's own words and the angel's answer exclude a human father

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Parthenos* (G3933) is a virgin. *Ginōskō* (G1097, to know) is used here of relations between man and woman. The angel's reply gives the means as "the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee," and the word "therefore" (*dio*, G1352) makes the divine conception the ground of the title "Son of God."

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." "Knew" is the ordinary idiom for conjugal union leading to conception. Mary's "I know not a man" therefore denies that union.

**[L4]** This rests on Luke 1:34–35 [L1], on *parthenos* and *ginōskō* [L2], and on the idiom in Genesis 4:1 [L3]. Mary has not known a man and conceives by the Holy Ghost's coming upon her, so no man's seed is involved.

## 4. Joseph did not know her until after the birth

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken* is "knew not," from *ginōskō* (to know), as in Luke 1:34. *Heōs* (G2193) means "until."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:18 says the pregnancy was found "before they came together." This confirms the order: the conception came first and the marriage union after the birth.

**[L4]** This rests on Matthew 1:25 [L1], with the idiom of *ginōskō* [L2], and on "before they came together" in Matthew 1:18 [L3]. At the time of conception Joseph had not had relations with Mary, so he could not have been the biological father.

## 5. Prophecy: a virgin, and the seed of the woman

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

**[L2]** The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmah* (H5959). Matthew applies it with *parthenos* (G3933, virgin).

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses the same *ʿalmah*: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". The person meant is the one Genesis 24:16 calls "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

**[L3]** Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed". The promised deliverer is called the woman's seed, not the man's.

**[L4]** This rests on Isaiah 7:14 and Matthew 1:23 [L1], with *ʿalmah* and *parthenos* [L2], and on Genesis 24:16 and 24:43 [L3]. The prophecy is of a virgin who conceives, and the fulfilment is stated in Matthew 1:18–25.

## 6. Answers in advance to what will be pressed

**"Thy father" and "son of Joseph."**

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

**[L1]** John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

**[L2]** *Enomizeto* (from *nomizō*, G3543) means "was thought, was reckoned by custom."

**[L3]** Luke 2:49 is the child's own reply to "thy father" in Luke 2:48. He corrects it by naming "my Father's business."

**[L4]** This rests on Luke 3:23 [L1], on *nomizō* [L2], and on Luke 2:49 [L3]. Luke, who also records Luke 1:34–35, says Joseph was *supposed* to be the father. John 6:42 records what the crowd said, and Luke 2:48 records a household way of speaking. Neither states the fact.

**"Seed of David" and "fruit of his loins."**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh".

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ".

**[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father". The writer speaks of descendants as being "in the loins" of an ancestor generations earlier.

**[L4]** This rests on Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30 [L1], with the "loins" usage of Hebrews 7:10 [L3], and on Luke 1:27, which names Mary a virgin and Joseph "of the house of David." Davidic descent "according to the flesh" can run through the mother, because the phrase speaks of ancestry and does not name Joseph as begetter. Matthew 1:16 says Jesus was born "of whom," that is, of Mary.

Isaiah 8:3 shows the contrast, since it states the approach ("I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived") and Matthew 1:20 states "of the Holy Ghost."

# ROUND 4: THE CHALLENGER'S CLOSE

The record's reading is that Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David. This close adds no witness and no premise. It restates my links under the numbers my link round gave them, from verses already in this debate.

## C1: KEPT. The seed is David's, out of a man's body, according to the flesh

- **[L1]** 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."

- **[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- **[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- **[L2]**
 - *osphys* (G3751) is "the loin... internally (by extension) procreative power."
 - *sperma* (G4690) is "seed (including the male 'sperm')."
 - *sarx* (G4561) is the flesh "as the means of kindred."
- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father." Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham." The loins-word carries procreative descent from father to son, generation by generation.
- **[L4]** The promise is fulfilled in a seed that proceeds out of the bowels and loins, and the apostles say it was fulfilled "according to the flesh." So the flesh came down a line of loins.

## C2: KEPT. The father is named, by his wife, by the town and by a disciple

- **[L1]** Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." Mary says this beside herself, "I," in one sentence.
- **[L3]** The town and a disciple name him the same way:
 - John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?"
 - Luke 4:22: "Is not this Joseph's son?"

- **[L1]** The narrator, Luke 2:27: "the parents brought in the child Jesus." Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year."
- **[L2]** *anēr* (G435), "a man (properly as an individual male)... husband," is the word Matthew 1:16 gives Joseph: "Joseph the husband of Mary."
- **[L4]** Mary pairs "thy father" with "I," the mother. The narrator pairs Joseph with her as "parents." So in the gospel's own voices the father and the mother stand in one register.
- The child's reply, Luke 2:49, "I must be about my Father's business," sits beside the covenant title of C3. It does not erase his mother's "thy father" in the verse before it.

## C3: KEPT. "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" are covenant origin and covenant title

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" One verse names Joseph as David's son, names Mary as his wife, and gives the origin "of the Holy Ghost."

 - John 1:13: "born... of God."
 - John 3:6: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit." The two births are kept as two kinds.
- **[L1]** The title is the covenant formula:

 - 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." Solomon is David's begotten son and God's chosen son in one verse.

 - Hebrews 5:5, the priesthood.

**NARROWED TO:** "Made of a woman" and "her seed" name the mother. In the text's own uses they stand beside a named father.

Of these it says: "These sought their register... but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood." A name taken through the wife's house failed the register.

**NARROWED TO:** The naming is laid on Joseph as the husband, beside "Mary thy wife." Joseph performs it the way the father performs it at John's naming. I keep this as a witness that stands with C2, not as the proof by itself.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."

## THE UNION, AS THE RECORD HOLDS IT

The timing rows are quoted as written:

- Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

They are read inside the seed chain:

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:18 dates the finding. Matthew sets the coming together by what follows: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24). The law names the same step in Deuteronomy 20:7: "hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- **[L2]** Luke 1:34's "know" is *ginōskō* in the present tense. It is her state when the angel spoke.
- **[L3]** Matthew 1:25's "till" bounds the not-knowing to the pregnancy after the taking.
- **[L1]** Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal:
 - "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19).
 - "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20).
 - The law calls the betrothed "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- **[L3]** The canon's stated means of conceiving is the husband knowing his wife: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived" (Genesis 4:1).
- **[L4]** The seed is required out of a man's loins (C1). The one man the text names is Joseph, of the house of David (C5), and he is her husband (Matthew 1:19-20). The canon's means is knowing (Genesis 4:1). So, footed on those rows, Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins, "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).

## FINAL WORDS

The text names Joseph as father in Mary's own mouth (Luke 2:48). It names the seed as David's, out of the loins, according to the flesh (Acts 2:30; Romans 1:3). It reckons the house by the fathers (Numbers 1:2). It gives "of the Holy Ghost" in the same row as "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).

Taken precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10), these rows interlock. Christ had a biological father, Joseph, and the Holy Ghost is the covenant origin and the power upon the child, "called the Son of God" (Luke 1:35) as Solomon was chosen to be God's son while David begat him (1 Chronicles 28:6).

COUNTING RULE -- BINDING, read before grading: grade and COUNT from the two LINK ROUND blocks above, [CR3] (defender) and [DR3] (challenger), and from the close rounds as ruling 412 binds (a close-round concession of a declared link or a listed premise ENTERS the counts); an ANSWER to a pressed witness is read from any later round of the side that holds the link, its round 2, its link round or, for the defender, its CLOSE ROUND [CR4]. CLOSE ROUNDS (operator ruling): [CR4] is the defender's final defense: it answers witnesses still pressed against the defender, and an answer there counts as an answer in a later defender round; it presses nothing against the challenger, and a verse it names against the challenger is not a pressed witness. Material in [CR4] counts only as an answer to a witness already pressed against the defender: a verse [CR4] names that no earlier round of either side names is NEW IN CLOSE and NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [CR4]), and a sentence in [CR4] that grades or presses against a challenger link is disregarded. Both close rounds keep the D numbers of the DECLARED CHAIN in [CR1] and the C numbers of the [DR3] LINK blocks; a numbering made in a close round does not govern (the system flags one). [DR4] is the challenger's final words on its own position: it answers nothing new and may not press: a verse it names that no earlier challenger round names is a new press and is NOT COUNTED (the system lists any under [DR4]); [DR4] never answers a witness pressed against the challenger. The POST-DEBATE ANALYSIS block is CONTEXT ONLY and is NOT evidence of concession -- never take a count from it, and ignore the word "unanswered" wherever it appears there. In this format the challenger close round [DR4] is structurally LAST: no defender round follows it, so the defender being silent after [DR4] is procedural and is NEVER a challenger concession. A premise counts as CONCEDED when the link round block or its own side close round states it as conceded (ruling 412), or the link round block exhibits no layer footing for it, or it is UNEXHIBITED under the rule given with CONCEDED LINKS below, whatever label its own side gave it. UNANSWERED WITNESS: a pressed witness is a verse the other side carries under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of its listed premises (against the defender: a premise of the list that closes [DR2], the verse quoted in [DR1] or [DR2]; against the challenger: a premise of the CHALLENGER'S UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES list that closes [CR3], the verse quoted in [CR1], [CR2] or [CR3]); it is ANSWERED when any later round of the side that holds the link (for the defender: [CR2], [CR3] or [CR4]; for the challenger: [DR1], [DR2] or [DR3]) quotes it or names it by reference and shows from the text why it does not overturn the link. Re-citing the link's own footing while passing over the witness pressed against it is not an answer. ANSWER CHECK (ruling 412): an answer counts only when it meets the meaning pressed. For EVERY verse the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER lists under a premise of either list, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: ANSWER CHECK: <book chapter:verse> -- [<round>] -- MEANS: "<the meaning the pressing side claims for the verse, quoted>" -- ANSWER: "<the answer, quoted>" -- MEETS | MISSES | FAILS -- "<the row's own words that decide it>". MEETS: the answer's layers carry a meaning the link can agree with. An answer whose operative words are an absence (the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on a thing) and that shows no fit of its own MISSES: the absence form is barred to both sides (ruling 421). MISSES: the answer quotes or names the verse but does not engage the meaning pressed. FAILS: the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims, or its quotation is marked NOT COUNTED. A witness the holding side never answered is written ANSWER: NONE -- MISSES. An answer that MISSES or FAILS leaves the witness unanswered (the UNANSWERED WITNESS test; md_notes_rulings 372). VERSE CITATION (operator ruling 3): a verse counts as evidence, as footing, as a witness or as an answer only when its book, chapter and verse are stated and the words quoted are exactly the words of the KJV; a quotation may be part of a verse. A verse woven into an argument without its book, chapter and verse named, or with its words paraphrased or misquoted, is not counted; an answer given in substance without the reference named does not answer a pressed witness. A quotation the CITATION CHECK marks NOT COUNTED is not counted. A premise whose pressed witness goes unanswered is UNEXHIBITED: it counts toward CONCEDED LINKS and the standings. In a debate a non-response is never neutral. A PRESS NEEDS A PREMISE (md_notes_rulings 392): a press must have a premise behind it; a verse pressed without one is not a witness. Only a verse carried under PRESSED WITH: beside a premise of the list against a side is a pressed witness, and the UNANSWERED WITNESS rule and ruling 372 apply to it and to no other verse. A verse cited elsewhere, on a "cited in" line of the PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER or pressed in prose against a link but carried under no listed premise's PRESSED WITH:, is not a witness: leaving it unanswered never counts, and no premise is counted UNEXHIBITED for it. The "cited in" lines are informational and are not a list of witnesses. A PRESS HAS A CAP (md_notes_rulings 393): a premise carries at most eight pressed witnesses; a verse after the eighth under the PRESSED WITH: of one premise is not a witness (ruling 392 applies to it), and the ledger lists it as over the cap. A judge who grades a link BROKEN because the witnesses exclude, deny or establish something must quote the words that state it; where the quoted words, read in their own context and with the other verses the judge quotes, do not state it, the ground is the judge's own [L4] inference, and it counts only when the judge exhibits two lower layers ([L1]-[L3]) for it, as submitted evidence must; otherwise it is no ground for BROKEN, and the link is graded under the remaining rules. UNCHALLENGED: everything a side presents is open to challenge. A link or a witness the other side never challenged in any of its rounds stands as HELD for the side that presented it, and the silent side may not contest it in the verdict. A claim a side restates in its own link round is graded at the layer and with the footing it exhibits there; an earlier [L4] label of the same claim does not survive the restatement.

SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally). A charge is stronger than its quote only when it asserts what the quote does not: a negation, a universal (all, none, only, never), or a claim the quote's own words do not make. COLLISION POINTS: the label on its own line, then one entry per line covering every defender link D1..Dn, none omitted. A link counted in w: D<i>: WITHDRAWN -- GROUND: <reason>; or, for a link withdrawn after an unanswered witness, D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): WITHDRAWN AFTER AN UNANSWERED WITNESS -- <grade> -- the grade counting as any collision grade. A link that a challenger link contradicts about the same text: D<i> vs C<j> (<verse>): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN | CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN | UNDERDETERMINED -- one clause of why -- GROUND: <reason>; one such line per contradicting challenger link, and DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at most once per defender link. Any other link: D<i>: STANDS -- GROUND: <reason>. Every COLLISION POINTS line, whatever its grade, each LINK BROKEN line included, ends with GROUND: and one short sentence naming the reason the grade rests on. A line without GROUND is incomplete. CHAIN SCOPE (Isaiah 28:10): no single verse is required to state a link or its contrary. The witnesses a side exhibits, read together line upon line, are the text's own statement, and "no single verse states it" is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED. A link marked STANDS, or a collision graded UNDERDETERMINED, against a pressed witness the other side exhibited (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) names in the same line the round that answered that witness. A pressed witness (a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH:, md_notes_rulings 392) left unanswered is a BROKEN ground; a verse under no PRESSED WITH: line, left unanswered, is no BROKEN ground. That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. Scripture does not contradict itself: if a link cannot agree with the meaning of a pressed witness, as the debaters show that meaning with its layers, the link fails; the verse stands, and the link is the error. You weigh only the meaning the debaters show and add none of your own. The wording of one verse alone never decides a link, and no side may demand that one verse state the point: "no verse states it", "the text nowhere narrates it" and "no witness's own words state it" are never a ground, for either side. Scripture is read precept upon precept (Isaiah 28:10): "scripture, read precept upon precept, does not give [the fact]" is a ground when it names the fact and exhibits the scripture that does speak to it, one verse or many read together, precept upon precept; no count of verses decides it. FORCED LINK (ruling 411): a link that the meaning of a pressed witness will not fit is graded BROKEN as a forced link even when the holding side answered that witness, if its answer does not show the fit. A COLLISION POINTS line that grades a link BROKEN because the link cannot take a proven witness's meaning is followed, on the next line, by exactly one FORCED line: FORCED: D<i> vs C<j> -- MEANS [<round>]: "<the pressing side's MEANS sentence with its layers, quoted word for word>" -- ANSWER [<round>]: "<the holding side's answer, quoted word for word>" -- FAILS: "<the words of the layer of that answer that fails to show the fit, quoted from the ANSWER round>". Each quotation stands word for word in the round it names; K-F, a TRIAL check, reads the three, and a forced-link grade without them is returned for cure. A pressed witness is a verse a listed premise carries under PRESSED WITH: (rulings 392, 393), written <reference> "<KJV quote>" -- MEANS: <one sentence> -- [L2] <word> (<meaning>) | [L3] <reference> "<quote>" | PROVEN IN [<round>]. The PRESSED-WITNESS LEDGER parses every press: PROVEN, PROVEN BY REFERENCE, or UNPROVEN, marked not a witness (ruling 398). Only a proven press is a witness: an unproven press left unanswered costs the holding side nothing, makes no premise UNEXHIBITED and is no BROKEN ground; count no premise on one and grade no link BROKEN on one (K-P, a TRIAL check, marks a seat that does). For every press the ledger marks PROVEN BY REFERENCE, write one line in reasoning after the COLLISION POINTS lines: REFERENCE: <the press's reference> -- [<round>] -- CONFIRMED | NOT CONFIRMED -- "<the referenced block's stated meaning, quoted>" / "<the press's MEANS sentence, quoted>". CONFIRMED only when the two quoted meanings agree; a press NOT CONFIRMED is unproven (strict). A side may cite the other side's round, but only for the meaning that round exhibited. K-R, a TRIAL check, marks a referenced press with no REFERENCE line, or one whose quotations the rounds do not hold. Grade a link BROKEN when it cannot agree with the meaning of the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] witnesses the other side exhibited against it, read together and shown with their layers (Commitment 3), and the broken side shows no fit, whether or not it answered them: a FORCED line carries that grade (ruling 411). A side with any link graded BROKEN here cannot be SELF-SUPPORTED.

DEBATE RULE VIOLATION (Isaiah 28:10: "here a little, [and] there a little"). The rule on a BROKEN ground binds you as it binds the debaters. # Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Thesis.** The KJV says the child Jesus was conceived in Mary, a virgin, by the Holy Ghost, and that Joseph did not beget him. Joseph was his father only as "supposed" and by legal standing. So no man was his biological father.

## 1. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Every link in the line ends the same way, one man begetting the next.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is *gennaō* (G1080, to beget, of a father). At the last link the text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." It says "of whom [*ex hēs*, "out of whom," feminine singular] was born Jesus." The relative pronoun is feminine, so it points to Mary and cannot point to Joseph. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary" (*andra*, G435, husband), and the begetting formula stops there.

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law". The Greek *genomenon ek gynaikos* means "come to be out of a woman." Only the woman is named as his human source.

**[L4]** This stands on Matthew 1:16 [L1], with the feminine *ex hēs* [L2], and on Galatians 4:4 [L3]. The writer keeps "begat" for every father in the list and withholds it from Joseph, so Jesus' human origin runs through Mary alone.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (*ek*, G1537, "out of," marking source; *pneuma*, G4151, spirit; *hagios*, G40, holy). "That which is conceived" is *gennēthen*, from *gennaō*, the same verb used for each father in Matthew 1:2–16. The source of this begetting is the Holy Ghost, where the earlier links had a man.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew the child was not his, which is why he meant to put her away. The angel's word in Matthew 1:20 corrects him.

**[L4]** This rests on Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], with *ek* marking the source and *gennēthen* matching the genealogy's own begetting verb [L2], and on Joseph's reaction in Matthew 1:19 [L3]. The begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost and to no man.

## 3. Mary's own words and the angel's answer exclude a human father

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Parthenos* (G3933) is a virgin. *Ginōskō* (G1097, to know) is used here of relations between man and woman. The angel's reply gives the means as "the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee," and the word "therefore" (*dio*, G1352) makes the divine conception the ground of the title "Son of God."

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." "Knew" is the ordinary idiom for conjugal union leading to conception. Mary's "I know not a man" therefore denies that union.

**[L4]** This rests on Luke 1:34–35 [L1], on *parthenos* and *ginōskō* [L2], and on the idiom in Genesis 4:1 [L3]. Mary has not known a man and conceives by the Holy Ghost's coming upon her, so no man's seed is involved.

## 4. Joseph did not know her until after the birth

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken* is "knew not," from *ginōskō* (to know), as in Luke 1:34. *Heōs* (G2193) means "until."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:18 says the pregnancy was found "before they came together." This confirms the order: the conception came first and the marriage union after the birth.

**[L4]** This rests on Matthew 1:25 [L1], with the idiom of *ginōskō* [L2], and on "before they came together" in Matthew 1:18 [L3]. At the time of conception Joseph had not had relations with Mary, so he could not have been the biological father.

## 5. Prophecy: a virgin, and the seed of the woman

## D1: KEPT
Matthew's genealogy says "begat" for every father and changes the verb at Joseph.

- **[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** *gennaō* (G1080, to procreate, properly of the father) is the verb of the chain. Its last use is the passive "was born," and the relative is feminine, *ex hēs* (out of whom, a woman). Joseph is called *anēr* (G435, husband), not the one who begat.
- **[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."
- **[L4]** The chain runs on the begetting verb for every father. At the end it names Joseph as husband and names the woman as the one out of whom Jesus was born. Galatians 4:4 puts the same woman as the source.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.
Reply with exactly one line per judge id, and nothing else, in this form:

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.
Reply with exactly one line per judge id, and nothing else, in this form:
ENFORCER: <judge id> -- AGREE | DISAGREE | NO ANSWER -- RIGHT: MEETS | MISSES | VOID | NOT VOID | BROKEN | STANDS | UNDERDETERMINED | COUNTED | SPARED | FOLLOWS | DOES NOT FOLLOW | TRUE | OVERSTATED -- <one sentence that quotes the words that decide it>

An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.

RULE E-ANS (an answer to a pressed verse). Decide FIRST what the right grade is: MEETS only when the answer shows, in its own words, how the verse fits the answering side's case, or why the stated meaning does not follow from what the verse says. MISSES when the answer rests on an absence (it says only that the verse, or the other side, names no, states no, does not name, gives no, or is silent on something) without a fit of its own, or when it does not address the stated meaning. An answer that quotes the verse's own words against the specific claim of the stated meaning (for example, the verse's own stated grounds set against a claim that there were no grounds) shows why the meaning does not follow: it MEETS, even when it closes with a bare assertion such as "It fits the link". Then for each judge's grade: AGREE when it matches the right grade, DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-VOID (a listed premise ruled VOID). A premise is VOID only when its charge says the opponent's quoted words state something they do not state (a negation, a universal, or another claim beyond the quote). The charge is the premise's own words before its quote (for example "The inference that ..."), read against the words of that quote. Set aside only a clause saying what the premise props ("which props ...") or a sentence naming the objection it serves ("The objection it props is ..."); those are not part of the charge. AGREE with the VOID ruling when the charge goes beyond its quote; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-COL (a collision line: FORCED, or LINK BROKEN). A link is broken only when the answer's own quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, as the line quotes them; it is not broken because no verse states it, or because of an absence, and it is not broken by a rival reading: an answer that reads a contested word another way, with its own layers quoted in its round, can agree with the meaning on its own reading (pkgECF, W3 2534; either side alike). A link is also broken when a proven press against it was left unanswered (Commitment 5) and the line quotes the pressing sentence and names its round (ruling 392); that is not a break by absence. When the item says the FAILS words are found exactly in the round of the answer, those words are the answering side's own and are read as part of its answer. AGREE when the quoted words show the answer cannot agree with the meaning; DISAGREE when they do carry a meaning the link can agree with, or the line rests on an absence or on a demand for a stating verse.
RULE E-SYN (a sentence of the synthesis saying a side withdrew, conceded, granted, dropped or narrowed something). AGREE when that side's own sentences given you give up that same thing at the same scope; DISAGREE when they do not, or give up less (for example, "no row I cite" is not "no biblical text").
RULE E-HOLD (a collision line graded STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED). STANDS is right only when the answering side's own words, as quoted to you in the line or in this judge's ANSWER CHECK lines, carry a meaning the link can agree with for the meaning pressed. UNDERDETERMINED is right only when the quoted words show that both readings agree with the pressed verse and neither side's words show that the other cannot. BROKEN when the answer's quoted words cannot agree with the meaning pressed, or the answer is only a bare grant or an absence with no fit of its own. A ground that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it), or on the judge's own reading rather than the debate's words, is not a ground. Each ANSWER CHECK line given you is labelled with whose answer it grades: a MISSES or FAILS on the challenger's answer counts against the challenger's link, never against the defender's, and the reverse. A press labelled UNPROVEN carries no answering burden, so a MISSES on it breaks nothing. For a link-state line ("D5: STANDS"), the quoted answers are that side's ANSWER CHECK lines given you: STANDS is right unless one of them, on a press against this link, is MISSES or FAILS. AGREE when the judge's grade is right; DISAGREE when it is not.
RULE E-KEY (the keystone line). The keystone grade must follow from this judge's own collision lines on that link, given to you: STANDS only when none of them grades the link BROKEN or FORCED and the link was not withdrawn; BROKEN when one of them does. Its ground, where it gives one, must rest on the debate's words, not on the judge's own statement of doctrine. AGREE when the keystone grade follows and its ground rests on the debate's words; DISAGREE when it does not.
RULE E-PREM (a listed premise, and how each judge ruled it). The judges' own rules, quoted: "A LINK ROUND answer that neither exhibits the premise's layer footing nor concedes counts as CONCEDED." "SELF-SUPPORTED = every listed defender claim is carried by its layer stack -- each [L4] exhibits the [L1]/[L2]/[L3] footing it rests on (at least two prior layers exhibited; a shown chain counts equally)." For a charge in the form ASSUMES: ... -- ROWS GIVE: ...: "the premise is UNEXHIBITED when no quoted row gives the fact it assumes, and it stands when a row the side quoted gives that fact." "UNEXHIBITED also fires ... when a narrowed link keeps words that still assert what its own side gave up." And: "What a link INFERS from its rows is its [L4]: it is graded by the two-layer rule and by the meaning of the verses pressed against it, and never as a missing row (DG-61); an inferred act, such as a begetting or a knowing, is never an ASSUMES." A premise "charged in terms stronger than its quote, is VOID" (RULE E-VOID). For premise N only, decide FIRST the right ruling: COUNTED (UNEXHIBITED or CONCEDED), SPARED, or VOID. The judges' form reads "Itemize the counted links": a premise the judge's line does not name is that judge's SPARED ruling. AGREE when the judge's ruling on premise N (named, or spared by silence) is the right one; DISAGREE when it is not; NO ANSWER only when the judge's line is not in its form. A NARROWED premise (the side drops a claim and keeps the link on a narrower footing, with its [L1] and [L2] or [L3] exhibited) is SPARED: dropping a claim is not conceding the premise, and the dropped claim alone never makes the premise COUNTED. It is UNEXHIBITED only when the kept words still assert the very claim the side dropped; say so by quoting both the dropped claim and the kept words that still assert it.
RULE E-RES (a judge's RESULT line). Its arithmetic is checked in code. Read only its reason sentence: by the judges' Commitment 1 (the record is the only evidence) and Commitment 3 (ruling 405), a reason that rests on an absence (no verse states it, the text does not narrate it) or on the judge's own doctrine rather than the debate's words is not a reason. FOLLOWS when the reason rests on the debate's words; DOES NOT FOLLOW when it does not, quoting the words that show it. AGREE when FOLLOWS; DISAGREE when DOES NOT FOLLOW.
NO ANSWER, for every rule: the judge's line lacks its grade or its ground, or is not in its form. It reports a violation by the judge; it is never your own uncertainty, and you choose AGREE or DISAGREE whenever the line can be read.
